title: Casper and the Witness
premise: Retired detective Ines Oyelaran buys a missing woman's diary at an estate sale, only to find entries written after the date of her disappearance. The trail leads to the Halvard family's annual anniversary dinner, where a fortune hangs on the legal fiction that Marguerite Halvard is dead. As Ines closes in on the living witness everyone buried, she must choose between exposing a family's crime and protecting the frightened woman who trusted her with the truth. At the dinner, Ines forces the confession into the open, and Marguerite chooses to testify, trading her inheritance for her name.
about_author: Juniper Iversen is a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade transcribing other people's worst days before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who refuse to stay quiet, from a coastal cottage shared with an opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Ines Oyelaran, running her failing bookshop in the rain-grey town of Marrow Bay, catalogues an estate lot and finds Marguerite Halvard's diary—its final entry dated three weeks after her official disappearance. Haunted by old cases and new debts, Ines begins reading against every instinct to stay invisible herself. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: reluctant reawakening; the detective's hunger stirring after years of dormancy.

chapters.title: A Glass Raised to the Dead
chapters.summary: Ines infiltrates the Halvards' anniversary memorial dinner under the pretext of selling rare books, meeting the cold patriarch Edmund and his watchful daughter-in-law Celeste. Every toast to Marguerite's memory feels rehearsed, and one guest—a nervous cousin named Tobias—flinches when Ines mentions the diary. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: rising dread and suspicion; the polished grief of wealth hiding something rotten beneath.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Buried
chapters.summary: Following Tobias's panicked tip, Ines tracks Marguerite to a convent hospice up the coast, where she has hidden as a volunteer under a false name. Marguerite confesses: she faked her death to escape Edmund, who killed her husband over the inheritance—but her diary, left behind in haste, is proof she lives. POV: alternating Ines and Marguerite. Emotional beat: terror giving way to fragile trust between two women who chose survival.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Toast
chapters.summary: Edmund's men close in on the hospice, forcing Ines and Marguerite back to Marrow Bay on the night of the final dinner. Ines engineers a confrontation before the assembled family, producing the diary and goading Edmund into a half-confession that Tobias records. Police arrest him; Marguerite publicly renounces her inheritance and takes back her name. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: catharsis and cost—justice won outside the law, love chosen over duty, and a bookshop that finally feels like home.
